---
title: "The Project Charter"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** Write the Brief. Who Said What is advised. **Objective:** give the agent standing instructions for a project, and know where they end and enforcement begins.
**Time:** about 15 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">Last verified (docs, not run): Claude Code v2.1.323 and OpenCode docs (they describe V2; installed version not checked) on 2026-11-13 (sources in `research/forest-and-reef.md` and `research/doctor.md`).</span>
:::

Typing the same background every session is wasteful. A **project instructions file** is read at the start so the agent already knows the project's conventions.

::: {.panel-tabset group="companion"}

## Claude Code

The file is `CLAUDE.md`. It can live in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (all your projects), `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md` (the project, shared if committed), and `./CLAUDE.local.md` (yours, not committed). Files in the working directory and above are loaded at launch, and ones in subdirectories are loaded when needed. `/init` drafts one from your project and `/memory` lists and edits them. `@path` imports another file, and the imported text still uses context.

## OpenCode + Ollama

The file is `AGENTS.md` in the project root (or `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` for all projects). `/init` creates or updates it. The `instructions` array in `opencode.json` adds more files. OpenCode also falls back to `CLAUDE.md` if there is no `AGENTS.md`.

:::

## What goes in, and the limit

Put in facts the agent cannot guess: how to run the tests, where data lives, naming conventions, "never edit `raw/`". Keep it short (the Claude Code docs aim for under 200 lines per file) because very long instructions are followed less well.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Instructions are advice.** Claude Code's docs describe `CLAUDE.md` as context, and not as enforced configuration. A line saying "never delete files" cannot stop a delete. Enforcement comes from permission rules, hooks, or managed settings (organisation-set rules you cannot override): the carapace you built in the Crypt.
:::

Instruction files go stale too: a rule written for an older model, a path that no longer exists, two files that disagree. The docs warn that when instructions contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily. In Claude Code (v2.1.283 or later), `/doctor prompt-audit` (`/doctor` is a **bundled skill**, a ready-made skill that ships inside the tool) checks your instruction files for outdated or conflicting content and writes a report with proposed edits. It changes nothing until you ask. It checks content only, so size and cost are out of scope. The audit is itself a model reading your files, so review its suggestions like any other output. Not checked: an OpenCode equivalent.

The AI for Science best practices (a European draft with no endorsements yet; practice 5) make a related point for your own code and notebooks: an agent operates a tool or dataset from its docstrings and descriptions, so write them as if an agent will re-run the work. Put units, data versions and assumptions in the docstring or next to the code. Their example is a renamed parameter with an old docstring: the agent called a name that no longer existed. The page also warns that stale documentation leads to plausible but wrong results. Not checked first-hand: read 2026-11-20 through a fetch summary, so re-check the wording on the page; see `research/aiforscience.md`.

Write the file yourself first and read what `/init` produces critically. A generated file can contain wrong guesses about your project.

<div data-ao-honour="write-charter" data-xp="15">Write a short instructions file (about ten lines) for one of your real projects: how to run its tests, where data lives, and one thing the agent should leave alone.</div>

## Lore

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [AI for Science, practice 5: documentation and data for agents](https://aiforscience.eu/best-practices/05-documentation-and-data-for-agents/): AI for Science (European draft best practices), docs. Why read: it argues that precise, current docstrings, units and metadata are what agents work from. A draft with no endorsements yet; it also mentions llms.txt, which it calls a proposal that no body has ratified.
- [How Claude remembers your project](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it covers CLAUDE.md placement, AGENTS.md and auto memory, and describes these as context that guides the agent.
- [Best practices for Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it shows what belongs in an instructions file and what to enforce another way.
- [Hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks): Anthropic, docs. Why read: hooks are the way to enforce a rule that an instructions file can only request.
- [Rules](https://opencode.ai/docs/rules/): OpenCode, docs. Why read: it explains AGENTS.md and the instructions setting for the OpenCode side.
:::
